title: Tinman driver protocol message
description: One newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 message exchanged with the Tinman driver on stdin and stdout, per the specification at https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification. Tinman defines no wire protocol of its own: a client in any language reaches for an existing JSON-RPC library, and the language servers, debug adapters and model-context servers a test author already runs speak the same framing. A protocol fault is an `error` object carrying a reserved code. A failed expectation is not a protocol fault, because the call succeeded and the product disagreed, so it returns a `result` whose `ok` is false. Referenced by features/driver-protocol.feature.

request.description: A call from the test runner to the driver. The parameters a method requires are constrained here rather than on the params object, because params alone cannot see which method it belongs to. A driver holds several sessions at once, so an omitted session on a call that addresses one is ambiguous rather than defaultable.

id.description: Client-assigned call identifier, echoed on the reply. Tinman assigns it no meaning beyond correlation.

method.description: The operation called. A method outside this set is answered with the reserved code -32601.

params.description: Arguments for the called method. Which of these each method requires is constrained by the request definition's conditional branches, because that is the only place the method name is in scope. Declaring a property here permits it; it never requires it.

session.description: The session the call addresses. Absent on launch, which creates one.

command.description: The target command, on a launch call.

sandbox.description: Backend-neutral sandbox specification for the session, on a launch call. Omitted means the secure defaults.

as.description: The name the captured collection is bound to, on a capture call.

response.description: A reply from the driver. Exactly one of result or error is present, per the JSON-RPC specification.

result.description: The outcome of a call the driver was able to make. A failed expectation reports here rather than as an error, because the call itself succeeded.

ok.description: Whether the operation did what it was asked. False on a failed expectation or a locator that did not resolve.

session.description: The session identifier, on a launch reply.

failure.description: What went wrong, when ok is false. Names what was looked for and what was found, so the client reports without a second call.

screen.description: The rendered screen, on a screen reply and on a failure that shows what the step saw.

tom.description: The terminal object model, on a tom reply. Conforms to the tom schema.

backend.description: The sandbox backend the session runs under, on a sandbox reply.

items.description: The captured items, on a capture reply, in screen order.

error.description: A protocol fault, per the JSON-RPC specification's error object. Reserved codes carry their standard meanings: -32700 parse error, -32600 invalid request, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal error. Tinman defines no codes of its own, because a fault outside that set is a product outcome and belongs in a result.

data.description: What the fault concerned, such as the unknown method name.
